Description: Customer asks to cancel all or part of an order they placed, or to stop it from shipping. Signals: "cancel", "I no longer want", "ordered by mistake", "please stop this order". If the item has already been delivered and they want to send it back, use Return instead.

Customer asks to change or correct the shipping address on an order they already placed. Signals: "wrong address", "I moved", "update my shipping address", "ship to a different address". If this is a reply confirming an address we asked them to verify, use Address Verification Required instead.

Customer is replying to our email asking them to confirm a pre-order. Signals: subject starts with "Re:", quoted text from our pre-order confirmation email, the customer confirming they still want the item or asking to cancel it in response. Do not use for questions about when a placed pre-order will ship (use Where is my order?) or pre-purchase stock questions (use Product Inquiry).

Customer is replying to our email asking them to verify their shipping address. Signals: subject starts with "Re:", quoted text from our address verification request, the customer confirming or correcting the address in response. Rarely the first email in a thread. A customer asking to change an address on their own initiative is Address Change.

Customer is replying to our email asking them to verify an order (for example identity, payment or order details). Signals: subject starts with "Re:", quoted text from our order verification request, the customer confirming the order, sending ID or answering our verification questions. Rarely the first email in a thread.

Customer is replying to our email asking them to confirm the size on an order. Signals: subject starts with "Re:", quoted text from our size verification request, the customer confirming or changing the size in response. Rarely the first email in a thread. A pre-purchase sizing question is Product Inquiry.

Customer asks where their order is or when it will arrive. Signals: "where is my order", "has it shipped", "no tracking", "when will I get it", "tracking hasn't updated", or a question about when a placed pre-order will ship. Must come from the customer. If tracking shows delivered but they don't have it, use Delivered Not Received.

An email from a carrier, brand or retail partner (not the customer) about the shipping status of an order: delays, delivery exceptions, held packages, returned-to-sender notices or updated delivery dates. Signals: sender is a carrier or partner, automated shipping language. A customer asking about their order status is Where is my order?

Customer says the order shows as delivered but they did not receive it. Signals: "says delivered but", "never arrived", "not at my door", "package missing", "stolen". Takes precedence over Where is my order? whenever tracking is described as delivered.

Customer received an item that is damaged, defective, dirty or showing wear. Signals: "arrived damaged", "broken", "torn", "stained", "defective", photos of damage. If the item is undamaged but not what they ordered, use Wrong Item Received.

Customer received a different item than they ordered: wrong product, size, color or quantity, or an item missing from the package. Signals: "not what I ordered", "wrong size sent", "wrong color", "missing item". If the size they ordered simply doesn't fit, use Return.

Customer wants to send an item back or needs return instructions or a label, including for items that don't fit or they don't like, and including requests to return a final-sale item that has already been delivered. Signals: "return", "send back", "return label", "exchange", "doesn't fit". If they already sent it back and are asking about the money, use Refund.

Customer has already returned or cancelled something and is asking about the status or amount of their refund. Signals: "where is my refund", "haven't been refunded", "refund status", "wrong refund amount". If the question is specifically about a fee deducted from the refund, use Return Fee. If they want to return something and haven't yet, use Return.

Customer is replying to our email asking them to confirm they accept that an item is final sale. Signals: subject starts with "Re:", quoted text from our final-sale confirmation email, the customer accepting or declining in response. Rarely the first email in a thread. A request to return a delivered final-sale item is Return.

Questions or requests about the customer's Editorialist account: login, password reset, changing account email or details, unsubscribing or email preferences. Do not use for account deletion or personal data requests (use Legal - Privacy Request).

Pre-purchase questions about a product: sizing and fit advice, materials, availability, restocks, whether an item can be pre-ordered, authenticity, or product details. Signals: the customer has not ordered the item yet. Questions about an item already ordered usually belong to an order type.

Customer asks about or disputes customs, duties, import taxes or VAT charged on an international order, including being asked to pay duties at delivery. Signals: "customs", "duties", "import tax", "VAT", "DHL wants me to pay".

Customer asks about or disputes a fee charged for a return, such as a return shipping or restocking fee deducted from their refund. Signals: "return fee", "restocking fee", "why was I charged for the return", "deducted from my refund".

Customer asks about or disputes shipping charges on an order or before buying: cost, free shipping thresholds, expedited shipping prices. Signals: "shipping cost", "why was I charged shipping", "free shipping". Customs and import charges are Duty Fee.

General feedback about Editorialist with no specific order problem to solve: complaints about the service, site or experience overall, praise, or suggestions. If the customer is unhappy about a specific issue (delay, damage, refund, etc.), use that issue's type instead, regardless of tone.

A copyright or DMCA takedown notice, typically about images, text or other content on our site. Signals: "DMCA", "copyright infringement", "takedown notice", "17 U.S.C. 512", a rights holder or their lawyer identifying copyrighted material.

A brand, rights holder or their representative asking us to remove product listings, for example for trademark, counterfeit, unauthorized reselling or distribution reasons. Signals: "remove our products", "unauthorized retailer", "trademark", "counterfeit", sender represents a brand. Copyright claims about content are Legal - DMCA request.

A request about personal data: delete my account or data, access or export my data, opt out of data sale or sharing, or questions citing GDPR, CCPA or other privacy laws. Signals: "delete my account", "delete my data", "GDPR", "CCPA", "do not sell". Simple marketing unsubscribes are Account Inquiry.

A payment dispute, from either a payment processor or a customer. Includes chargeback or dispute notices from processors (Stripe, PayPal, Affirm, Klarna, etc.), customers who don't recognize a charge or were charged twice, and customers who say they will dispute or have disputed the charge with their bank.
Someone applying for a job or internship, sending a resume or CV, or asking about open roles at Editorialist.
A journalist, publication or media outlet asking for comment, an interview, information or images for a story about Editorialist.

A brand, retailer, creator or affiliate proposing a partnership, collaboration, wholesale or affiliate relationship, or asking to be carried on Editorialist. A brand asking us to remove their products is Legal - Product Takedown Request.

Automated notifications from software tools and services we use: system alerts, billing or renewal notices, account security notices, integration errors or app updates. Shipping status emails from carriers or partners are Delivery Update.

A newsletter, digest or publication email we are subscribed to, sent to a mailing list rather than to us personally. Signals: unsubscribe footer, list formatting, editorial or promotional content with no request for us.

Unsolicited sales or marketing outreach, cold pitches for services (SEO, lead generation, design, etc.), or obvious spam and phishing. Signals: generic greeting, sales pitch, no relationship to an order or customer issue.
The message is clear but fits none of the types above. Do not use this when you are unsure between types; in that case leave the type blank.
Never assign automatically. This type is set manually by agents only.
